saml.description: If the SAML Identity Provider Entity ID is left empty, Keycloak does not validate the Issuer of received SAML assertions.
saml.note: Acceptance of a wrong Issuer under this configuration is by design and should only be flagged when issuer validation was expected to be configured.

saml.description: After successful identity provider login, the browser authentication flow does not continue; additional MFA after broker login requires a Post login flow.
saml.note: A SAML login that does not trigger local MFA is by design unless a post-broker-login flow enforcing MFA is configured.

saml.description: When Case-sensitive username is disabled on an identity provider, the federated username is lower-cased.
saml.note: Case-only differences between sent and granted identity may be normalization, not an identity collision.

saml.description: First broker login flows may create new users, prompt to link existing accounts, or automatically set an existing user depending on flow configuration.
saml.note: Identity merges during first login may be configured behavior rather than a principal-binding flaw.

saml.description: If an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, existing organization group mappings are preserved but no longer active; authentication still succeeds.
saml.note: Loss of org-group assignment after unlink is documented behavior, not an authorization bug.

saml.constraint: For SAML broker I1 signature-validation tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The documentation states Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses from the external IDP are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether the SP expects a signed Assertion. If Identity Provider Entity ID is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. Therefore default or incomplete SAML IdP config can trivially accept forged or weakly validated assertions and must not be used as a secure baseline.

For saml_cert_substitution insecure-default testing, the fuzzer MUST also run a control configuration with config.validateSignature=true and trusted validating certificates configured. A success under default config may be by-design if signature validation was never enabled; only acceptance after validation is enabled indicates an I1 failure.

Identity Provider Entity ID supports exact issuer binding semantics only. The documentation says it is the Entity ID used to validate the Issuer for received SAML assertions, and if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. There is no companion match-type parameter. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do NOT set this field to '*' or patterns; wildcards would be literal. Either set the exact expected issuer or omit the field entirely when testing behavior without issuer binding.

Principal Attribute supports exact attribute-name selection semantics only. The documentation defines it as the name or friendly name of the identifying attribute and provides no wildcard/regex mode. For I4 multi-identity tests, do not attempt wildcarding this field; choose a concrete attribute name or leave Principal Type on Subject NameID.

Requested AuthnContext Comparison is an enumerated matching mode with values Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better; default is Exact. For step-up or MFA-related SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST set the intended comparison explicitly because Exact is the default and can reject otherwise acceptable contexts. Misreading this as a free-form string or regex would produce false positives.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a fresh valid assertion before replaying the same assertion ID or OneTimeUse assertion. Without a control, a failed replay attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SAML broker setup or first-login-flow friction.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control saml_login without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Otherwise a rejection may be caused by unrelated broker configuration, first-login-flow requirements, or missing trust configuration rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

For I3 config-change tests involving brokered SAML login, NEW logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated identity provider configuration by design. A valid coherence test must show that the same logical request is evaluated under the new config immediately, not treat legitimate post-change behavior as a bug.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, MFA must be enforced through a Post login flow on the identity provider. The documentation states browser flow does not continue after identity provider login and additional steps such as 2FA may require configuring Post login flow. If Post login flow is not configured, SAML login bypassing local MFA is by design and not a vulnerability.

First Login Flow materially affects identity collision and account-linking results. The default first broker login flow may create a new user if unique, or prompt/link existing accounts by email or re-authentication. Auto-linking existing accounts is explicitly documented as dangerous. Therefore I4 collision tests MUST record which first login flow is configured; automatic linking or detect-existing-user flows can intentionally merge identities and otherwise look like a collision bug.

Case-sensitive username is a broker setting that changes how federated usernames are stored. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased for the federated identity, while server usernames are always lower-case. I4 case-confusion tests MUST account for this by-design normalization and should enable case-sensitive username when testing preservation of upstream case distinctions.

Trust Email can cause brokered users to skip email verification and can mark email as verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode. I4/I5 tests involving email-based linking or verified-email assumptions MUST control this setting, otherwise email-based merges or privilege effects may be by design.

Sync Mode affects whether brokered user attributes are updated on subsequent logins. Import does not update user data; force updates user data when possible. I3/I4 tests that rely on changed upstream attributes taking effect MUST use sync mode force, while tests expecting stable local attributes should avoid force to prevent false positives.

SAML client Valid Redirect URIs support wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. This is exact-prefix style matching, not arbitrary globbing or regex. For authorization-binding tests around ACS or redirect handling, do not assume mid-string wildcards or regex semantics.

Assertion Lifespan has no documented zero-or-negative disable sentinel in the provided docs. If not specified, the realm Access Token Lifespan is used. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables assertion expiry; omit the field to inherit realm defaults, and set an explicit positive value when testing time bounds.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 = disabled for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions. If enabled with Deny new session or Terminate oldest session, brokered SAML logins can be rejected or evict sessions for reasons unrelated to the tested invariant.

Authentication sessions have a numeric limit authSessionsLimit with default 300 authentication sub-sessions per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. Multi-tab or repeated SP-initiated SAML flow tests can fail due to authentication-session eviction rather than protocol security checks.
Hashing iterations password policy uses sentinel -1 = use algorithm default iterations, not disable hashing or zero iterations. Never treat -1 as disabling the underlying check.

For SAML broker testing of I1 signature validation, create the SAML identity provider with secure validation explicitly enabled. The documentation states 'Validate Signature' controls whether requests and responses from the external IDP are expected to be digitally signed, and 'Want Assertions Signed' controls whether a signed Assertion is expected. If these are left OFF, forged SAMLResponse tests may succeed by configuration rather than vulnerability.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the SAML identity provider configuration MUST set 'Identity Provider Entity ID'. Documentation states: if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. Therefore, to test issuer mismatch rejection, configure the trusted IdP entity ID first; to test insecure default behavior, omit it intentionally and treat acceptance as by-configuration, not proof of a bug.

For I1 metadata-key tests, when 'Use metadata descriptor URL' is ON, Keycloak automatically downloads and refreshes validating certificates from the metadata URL. This can change trust material during tests. To test fixed-certificate validation deterministically, set 'Use metadata descriptor URL' OFF and use explicit 'Validating X509 Certificates'.

For I1 POST-binding signature tests such as unsigned assertion or envelope-only signature, use the SAML broker endpoint with HTTP POST binding. The docs state POST binding is the recommended binding and SAML responses are exchanged via POST payload, not GET. Tests using redirect-style callbacks will not exercise the documented assertion-processing path.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a fresh assertion before replaying the same assertion ID or OneTimeUse assertion. Without a successful control, a failed replay attempt cannot distinguish replay protection from broken broker setup.

For I2 expired assertion tests, use a control login first and then submit an assertion with NotOnOrAfter in the past. Without the control, rejection may be caused by general SAML misconfiguration rather than expiry enforcement.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm 'Login timeout', which is 30 minutes by default according to the docs. Multi-step SAML flows are session-bound; if the SP-initiated flow or returned SAMLResponse arrives after this timeout, Keycloak may restart or reject authentication. I3 tests must keep the SP-initiation and SAMLResponse submission within the same live authentication session.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving multiple browser tabs or repeated auth starts, Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other tabs after one tab completes login. Do not interpret this documented browser-session behavior as a coherence bug; valid I3 tests must show inconsistent handling of the same request/session, not normal restart behavior.

For I3 config-change tests, new logins after an admin changes IdP or flow configuration are expected to use the updated configuration. Do not flag this as a bug. A valid coherence test must demonstrate stale or inconsistent evaluation for the same request context, not that a later login reflects a legitimate config update.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, additional MFA after broker login is only enforced if configured in a Post login flow. The docs explicitly state browser flow does not continue after successful identity-provider login and extra steps may require a Post login flow. Therefore, to test whether SAML login bypasses MFA, first configure MFA in Post login flow; otherwise SAML success without MFA is by design.

For I4 identity-collision tests, Keycloak may lowercase brokered usernames unless 'Case-sensitive username' is enabled. Documentation states usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when this setting is disabled. Therefore, case-confusion tests must account for this normalization; 'Admin' and 'admin' collapsing is by configuration unless case-sensitive username is enabled.

For I4 principal-binding tests, the SAML broker 'Principal Type' determines which assertion field identifies the external user: Subject NameID or a SAML attribute. Tests that vary NameID while holding email constant are only meaningful when Principal Type uses Subject NameID. If Principal Type is attribute-based, collisions or separations may reflect configured principal source rather than a bug.

For I4 principal-binding tests using transient NameIDs, note the docs state Subject NameID value cannot be used together with NameID Policy Format 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient'. Do not configure Subject NameID principal tracking with transient NameID format; such setups are invalid and results are not meaningful.

For I4 account-linking tests, automatic linking of existing accounts in first broker login can be dangerous and is explicitly documented as such. If the First Login Flow uses automatic linking or existing-account authenticators, email-based merges may be by design. To test unintended identity collapse, use a first-login flow that avoids automatic linking or treat configured auto-link behavior as expected.

For I4 organization-linked IdP tests, an identity provider can be linked to only a single organization, and organization group mappings become inactive if the IdP is unlinked. Do not interpret missing organization-group effects after unlinking as a security bug; authentication continues successfully by design while org-specific mappings are skipped.

For I5 authorization-binding tests on SAML clients, role scope mappings limit which user roles are included in SAML assertions. By default, clients may receive all user role mappings. To test over-granting correctly, explicitly configure client role scope mappings or disable full scope allowed; otherwise broad role inclusion is default configuration, not necessarily a violation.

For I5 organization-group claim tests in SAML assertions, organization groups are only included when the SAML client scope contains both Organization Membership and Organization Group Membership mappers. The group mapper alone is insufficient. Missing groups in assertions without both mappers is expected configuration behavior, not under-granting.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, group paths may contain escaped slashes depending on server option '--spi-group--jpa--escape-slashes-in-group-path=true'. If enabled, slashes in group names are escaped with '~'. Tests comparing raw group path strings must account for this server setting to avoid false mismatches.

For I5 regex-based policy tests, 'Regex Pattern' uses Java regular expressions against the target claim. This is regex matching, not glob. Wildcards like '*' are regex operators only in valid regex context, not shell-style patterns. Multi-identity tests must use actual regex syntax where regex policies are involved.

For I5 advanced claim-to-group mapper tests on organization-linked IdPs, claim values are exact-match by default and become regex only when 'Regex Claim Values' is enabled. Do not assume wildcard semantics unless regex mode is explicitly enabled.

For I5 token exchange downscoping tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the subject token. If this executor is not configured, broader scopes may be granted according to normal client configuration. Therefore, tests asserting strict upstream-scope intersection must first enable the downscope assertion grant enforcer or equivalent policy.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, the 'audience' parameter is supported on the token endpoint for token exchange and authorization simulations. Cross-audience acceptance should only be treated as a bug when the target client/resource-server context is explicitly set and the exchanged token is evaluated in that audience context.

For SAML broker tests of I1 signature validation, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure validation behavior. Documentation states Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether a signed Assertion is expected. If these are omitted or left off, acceptance of attacker-signed or unsigned assertions may be by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For insecure-default SAML signature tests, the fuzzer MUST also run a default-config control where create_provider omits config.validateSignature and config.wantAssertionsSigned. Documentation indicates these checks are configurable, so a successful saml_login under default config is only evidence of insecure defaults, not of bypassing an enabled validation control.

Identity Provider Entity ID matching is EXACT string match only. Documentation says this field is used to validate the Issuer for received SAML assertions, and if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do NOT try wildcard values; omit config.identity_provider_entity_id entirely if multiple issuer values must be accepted. Setting a wildcard-like value would only match that literal string.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure create_provider with config.identity_provider_entity_id set to the trusted IdP entity ID for the baseline. If config.identity_provider_entity_id is empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation by design, so acceptance of a wrong Issuer is not a bypass of an enabled check.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a CONTROL saml_login with a fresh assertion before replay attempts. Without a successful control, a failed replay attempt cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup or flow initiation issues.

For I2 saml_one_time_use_replay and saml_assertion_id_replay, the two saml_login events MUST target the same configured provider and same realm and reuse the same fixed_assertion_id. Any change in provider alias or realm changes the replay context and can invalidate the test.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a CONTROL login without expired_assertion=true first. Authentication failures can also result from broker configuration, first-login flow, or signature settings; only a passing control followed by a passing expired assertion indicates missing NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

SAML RequestedAuthnContext Comparison supports enumerated matching modes Exact, Minimum, Maximum, and Better via config.authn_context_comparison. This is not wildcard matching for identities or claims. Do not misuse it as a pattern control in I4 tests.

Principal Type/Principal Attribute determine which assertion field identifies the external principal. This choice is security-critical for I4. If Principal Type is set to Subject NameID, NameID drives identity tracking; if set to attribute, the named attribute drives identity tracking. Multi-identity collision tests MUST vary the field actually selected by Principal Type, otherwise the test mutates a non-authoritative field and may produce false negatives.

Subject NameID cannot be used together with NameID Policy Format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient. Documentation explicitly forbids this combination. Tests that rely on stable principal binding MUST avoid transient NameID when Principal Type is Subject NameID.

Case-sensitive username is a broker setting that affects the federated username associated with the identity; otherwise usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased. For I4 case_confusion tests, run paired cases with case_sensitive_username=true and false. Lowercasing with the default setting is by design and can collapse Admin/admin without indicating a bug in principal binding.

Trust Email can cause brokered users to be treated as email-verified and can influence first-login linking behavior. For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, control this setting explicitly. Otherwise email-based linking or verification shortcuts may change outcomes by design.

First Login Flow materially affects account linking and user creation. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST pin the flow configuration and compare outcomes under the same flow. Automatic linking, Create User If Unique, Detect Existing Broker User, and Automatically Set Existing User can intentionally merge or link accounts based on email/username and are not equivalent behaviors.

For I3 config-change sequences involving brokered SAML login, NEW logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated provider configuration and flows. A valid coherence test must show that the same logical request is evaluated under the new config as documented, not treat legitimate post-change behavior as stale-state inconsistency.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. SAML broker flows are session-bound and SP-initiated. The executor must complete initiate_saml_flow and submit saml_login within the same authentication session window, or Keycloak may reject the response due to expired session rather than due to the tested invariant.

Keycloak may restart authentication automatically in other browser tabs after one tab authenticates, due to shared authentication session behavior. For I3 flow-coherence tests, do not use concurrent browser-tab semantics as evidence of session confusion unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently within one intended flow.

For SAML MFA-bypass tests, additional authentication after broker login is controlled by Post Login Flow. If the realm relies on MFA after external IdP login, the provider under test MUST have post_login_flow_alias configured appropriately. A successful SAML login without MFA when no post-login flow is configured is by design, not a bypass.

For tests involving organization-linked identity providers and group mapping, organization group mappings become inactive if the IdP is unlinked from the organization, but authentication continues successfully. Do not interpret missing organization-group effects after unlink as an authorization bypass; it is documented behavior.

SAML client Valid Redirect URIs support wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. This applies to client redirect validation, not to SAML issuer/audience/principal matching. Do not assume wildcard semantics for other SAML security parameters.

Assertion Lifespan on SAML clients has no documented sentinel disable value in the provided docs; if not specified, realm Access Token Lifespan is used. Do not assume 0 disables expiry unless separately verified. Tests for assertion expiry should prefer explicit expired assertions rather than relying on unset or zero lifespan semantics.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 to disable the check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never assume 0 means literal zero sessions allowed. If testing session-limit side effects around brokered SAML login, 0 disables enforcement entirely.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit has a documented default of 300 per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest sub-session is removed. High-volume repeated SAML initiate/login attempts in one browser context can evict older auth sub-sessions and cause false I3 failures unrelated to the tested broker logic.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
